heading: Menu actions
body:
An item with an `action` calls a method of an application service. Such a service is a Rust service in `client/services/` with `#[Lifetime({"value":"application"})]`. It starts with the app and stops when the app quits, so the method also works when no page is open. The `action` names the `service` (its type name) and the `method` (a method that takes only `&self`). Selecting the item never loads a page, so the page keeps its state: its fields, the text in its inputs and its scroll position.

To change the page, the application service forwards an event. It gets `CurrentPageEvents` by injection and calls `publish_event` with a model from `client/models`. Every live Rust page service with an `OnEvent` listener for that model receives it, as with any other event. A page service that two components share receives it once, and each prototype instance receives it once. `publish_event` answers `false` when the page has no listener. A listener cannot publish to the page again while it receives the event.

The optional `event` names the model that the method forwards. Tachyon uses it to decide when the item is enabled (see the next section). The build checks each action: the service must be a client Rust service with an application lifetime, the method must exist and take only `&self`, and the event must be a Rust model in `client/models`. Otherwise the build stops with `TY1370`.
